--- title: "Analysis" --- ::: key-takeaways ## Key Takeaways - The dataset includes **215 cargo movements** from **17 port authorities, 69 facilities and 180 different companies** with approximately 109 million metric tons of hazardous cargo reported in 2022. Geographic concentration is striking **İzmir (Aliağa), Adana (Ceyhan)** and **Hatay (İskenderun)** dominate the volume while most other provinces handle only a sliver of the total. - **Company-level tonnage is deeply uneven.** The bulk of receivers sit in the 10³–10⁴ ton range yet a handful of operators push well past 10⁷ and that gap matters enormously for policy. Just **107 of the 180 companies** clear the 20,000 ton threshold but together they move roughly **99.5% of all hazardous cargo.** Wide by headcount, narrow by liability. - A hypothetical **₺50/ton levy** on those threshold crossing companies would bring in around **₺5.4 billion** most of it coming from the top ten handlers alone. ::: ## 1. Overview of the dataset ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} overview <- hns2022 |> summarise( n_records = n(), n_ports = n_distinct(port_authority_short), n_facilities = n_distinct(facility), n_companies = n_distinct(company_clean), total_cargo_mt = sum(cargo_mt) ) overview ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: {.stat-grid} ::: {.stat-card} [215]{.value} [Records]{.label} ::: ::: {.stat-card} [17]{.value} [Port authorities]{.label} ::: ::: {.stat-card} [69]{.value} [Facilities]{.label} ::: ::: {.stat-card} [180]{.value} [Companies (cleaned)]{.label} ::: ::: {.stat-card} [108.9 M ton]{.value} [Total 2022 cargo]{.label} ::: ::: The dataset is a long table where each row pairs a **receiver company** with the **facility** that handled their cargo and the **regional port authority** that oversees that facility. The numeric column `cargo_mt` is what we'll be slicing in every direction below. ## 2. Where is hazardous cargo concentrated? Each port authority is mapped to its host province, and 2022 tonnage is summed accordingly. The darker the province, the heavier the load. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} prov_totals <- hns2022 |> group_by(iso2, province) |> summarise(total_mt = sum(cargo_mt), .groups = "drop") tr_states <- ne_states(country = "Turkey", returnclass = "sf") if ("iso_3166_2" %in% names(tr_states)) { tr_map <- tr_states |> left_join(prov_totals, by = c("iso_3166_2" = "iso2")) } else { norm <- function(x) tolower(stringi::stri_trans_general(x, "Any-Latin; Latin-ASCII")) tr_map <- tr_states |> mutate(name_n = norm(name)) |> left_join(prov_totals |> mutate(name_n = norm(province)), by = "name_n") } ggplot(tr_map) + geom_sf(aes(fill = total_mt), color = "white", linewidth = 0.35) + scale_fill_gradientn( colours = c("#F06292", "#EC407A", "#E91E63", "#C2185B", "#880E4F", "#3D0823"), na.value = "#9C8D88", labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale()), name = "Cargo (m. ton)" ) + coord_sf(crs = 4326) + labs( title = "Türkiye's hazardous cargo, 2022", subtitle = "Provinces are filled by the total tonnage handled at port authorities they host. Grey = no port authority in that province.", caption = "Source: Directorate General for Maritime Affairs, 2022. Author calculations." ) + theme_void(base_family = "Inter") + theme( plot.title = element_text(family = "Playfair Display", face = "italic", size = 22, color = "#3D0823", margin = margin(b = 6)), plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#3D0823", size = 12, margin = margin(b = 10)), plot.caption = element_text(color = "#3D0823", size = 10, hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 8)), legend.title = element_text(color = "#3D0823", face = "bold", size = 11), legend.text = element_text(color = "#3D0823", size = 10), legend.position = "right", plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFAF7", color = NA), panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFAF7", color = NA) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Total hazardous cargo handled in 2022, by host province of the port authority. The darker the province, the heavier the load.](analysis_files/figure-html/turkey-map-1.png){width=864} ::: ::: The Aegean coast dominates **İzmir** alone hosts both the **Aliağa and İzmir** port authorities, making it the single heaviest concentration on the map. The Eastern Mediterranean follows close behind with **Adana's Ceyhan** terminals and **Hatay's İskenderun** accounting for much of the remainder. The Black Sea, Marmara and Antalya regions are present but noticeably lighter. ## 3. How is cargo distributed across companies? Each company's 2022 tonnage is summed and plotted on a log scale to capture the full spread from the smallest handlers to the largest: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} company_totals <- hns2022 |> group_by(company_clean) |> summarise(total_mt = sum(cargo_mt), .groups = "drop") |> filter(total_mt > 0) ggplot(company_totals, aes(x = total_mt)) + geom_density(fill = "#FF80B0", alpha = 0.55, color = "#C2185B", linewidth = 1) + geom_vline(xintercept = 20000, linetype = "dashed", color = "#00C9D8", linewidth = 1) + annotate( "label", x = 20000, y = Inf, label = "20,000-ton threshold", vjust = 1.5, hjust = -0.05, color = "#00838F", fill = "#FFFAF7", label.size = 0, fontface = "bold" ) + scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) + labs( title = "Most companies are small. A handful are enormous.", subtitle = "Density of company-level total tonnage in 2022 (log-10 axis).", x = "Total cargo per company (metric tons, log scale)", y = "Density", caption = "Each company aggregated by its cleaned, deduplicated name." ) + theme_riyo() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning in annotate("label", x = 20000, y = Inf, label = "20,000-ton threshold", : Ignoring unknown parameters: `label.size` ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Density of total 2022 hazardous cargo tonnage per company (log scale). The cyan dashed line is the 20,000 ton policy threshold.](analysis_files/figure-html/density-companies-1.png){width=864} ::: ::: The pattern is hard to miss. Most companies cluster in the **10³–10⁴ ton** range, but a thin upper tail stretches well past **10⁷ tons** and that tail is where the real volume lives. On a linear axis, the smaller handlers would barely register; they outnumber the giants but are dwarfed by them in every other sense. ## 4. What would a tonnage levy actually cost? ( Hypothetical simulation) The Directorate is considering tax/regulatory measures targeting companies that exceed **20,000 tons** of hazardous cargo per year. To put a number on what that would mean, we apply a hypothetical **₺50 per ton** levy on the *full* tonnage of any company that crosses the threshold. > **Disclaimer.** ₺50/ton is illustrative — chosen for arithmetic clarity, not based on any draft policy. Treat absolute figures as proportions, not forecasts. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} TAX_RATE_TL_PER_TON <- 50 co_tax <- company_totals |> mutate( above_threshold = total_mt > 20000, tax_TL = if_else(above_threshold, total_mt * TAX_RATE_TL_PER_TON, 0) ) threshold_summary <- co_tax |> summarise( n_total = n(), n_taxed = sum(above_threshold), pct_companies = mean(above_threshold) * 100, total_mt = sum(total_mt), taxed_mt = sum(total_mt[above_threshold]), pct_taxed_mt = sum(total_mt[above_threshold]) / sum(total_mt) * 100, total_tax_TL = sum(tax_TL), total_tax_billion= sum(tax_TL) / 1e9 ) threshold_summary ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

c(threshold_summary$pct_companies, threshold_summary$pct_taxed_mt), below = c(100 - threshold_summary$pct_companies, 100 - threshold_summary$pct_taxed_mt) ) |> pivot_longer(c(above, below), names_to = "side", values_to = "pct") |> mutate(side = factor(side, levels = c("below", "above"), labels = c("Below 20k tons", "Above 20k tons"))) ggplot(share_df, aes(x = metric, y = pct, fill = side)) + geom_col(width = 0.55) + geom_text( aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct)), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 5, family = "Inter" ) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("Below 20k tons" = "#FFC1D8", "Above 20k tons" = "#C2185B")) + coord_flip() + labs( title = "Wide net, top-heavy bill.", subtitle = sprintf( "%.0f%% of companies cross the ````` ::: ::: ### Sensitivity to the threshold What if the threshold weren't 20,000 tons? The plot below traces how the **number of taxpayers** and the **share of tonnage taxed** move as we slide it. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} thresholds <- c(5e3, 1e4, 2e4, 5e4, 1e5, 2.5e5, 5e5, 1e6) sens <- tibble(threshold = thresholds) |> rowwise() |> mutate( n_taxed = sum(company_totals$total_mt > threshold), share_mt = sum(company_totals$total_mt[company_totals$total_mt > threshold]) / sum(company_totals$total_mt) * 100 ) |> ungroup() ggplot(sens, aes(x = threshold)) + geom_line(aes(y = share_mt), color = "#C2185B", linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point(aes(y = share_mt), color = "#C2185B", size = 3) + geom_text( aes(y = share_mt, label = sprintf("n=%d", n_taxed)), vjust = -1, color = "#00838F", fontface = "bold", size = 3.4, family = "Inter" ) + scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ",", scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 105), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) + labs( title = "How sharp is the cliff at 20,000 tons?", subtitle = "Even a 5x or 10x stricter threshold barely loses tonnage coverage — the giants dominate.", x = "Threshold (metric tons, log scale)", y = "Share of total tonnage above threshold", caption = "Annotations show the number of companies caught at each threshold." ) + theme_riyo() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Sensitivity of the policy to the threshold value.](analysis_files/figure-html/threshold-sensitivity-1.png){width=864} ::: ::: The take-away: because the upper tail is so heavy, **moving the threshold up by an order of magnitude barely reduces tonnage coverage** — but it sharply reduces the *number* of companies subject to the policy. That's a useful lever for designers who want a high-impact, low-friction policy. ## 5. Where do these companies handle their cargo? — port-authority breakdown ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} port_totals <- hns2022 |> group_by(port_authority_short) |> summarise(total_mt = sum(cargo_mt), .groups = "drop") |> arrange(desc(total_mt)) ggplot(port_totals, aes(x = fct_reorder(port_authority_short, total_mt), y = total_mt / 1e6)) + geom_col(fill = "#FF2D87", width = 0.65) + coord_flip() + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(suffix = " M ton")) + labs( title = "Aliağa and Ceyhan run away with it.", subtitle = "Total hazardous cargo handled in 2022, by regional port authority.", x = NULL, y = "Total cargo (million metric tons)" ) + theme_riyo() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Total hazardous cargo by port authority, 2022.](analysis_files/figure-html/port-bar-1.png){width=864} ::: ::: ## 6. Conclusions - **Geography:** Türkiye's hazardous cargo handling is **not evenly distributed**. A small set of provinces — driven by refining and large export terminals — dominates national volume. - **Industry structure:** The market is a **classic heavy-tailed distribution**. Many small handlers, a few giants moving most of the tonnage. - **Policy implication:** Because volume is so concentrated, a tonnage-based levy is **administratively narrow** — it would touch a minority of companies but capture most of the activity. That makes it both **easy to enforce** and **politically charged**. - **Sensitivity:** Moving the threshold from 20,000 to 100,000 or 200,000 tons would *not* meaningfully reduce coverage of total tonnage but would *significantly* reduce the number of regulated firms — a real lever for policy designers. Visit our [Data page](data.qmd) for documentation and the cleaned dataset, and the [Team page](team.qmd) to meet the people behind it.
